# Revision summary

This file is the clean post-revision version of the chikungunya INLA analysis.
It replaces the earlier exploratory `06_inla_spacetime_model.Rmd` workflow.

The main changes are:

1. **Study period fixed to January 2016 through December 2025** (120 monthly time points).
2. **All 5,570 Brazilian municipalities are retained in every month.**
   Municipality-months with no confirmed chikungunya notification are coded as
   `0 cases`, not `NA`.
3. **Confirmed chikungunya cases are defined by `CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13)`.**
4. **Population is modeled as `log(POP)` with an estimated coefficient**, not as
   a fixed offset.
5. The primary model remains:
   **negative binomial + BYM2 space + monthly RW2 time + municipality-month IID
   Type I space-time interaction**.
6. Sensitivity analyses are separated from the primary fit:
   Poisson likelihood; exclusion of 2020-2021; and a Center-West
   Type I versus Type IV interaction comparison.
7. Pearson residuals use the **negative-binomial variance**, not the Poisson
   approximation.
8. Absolute-incidence checks use the **same confirmed-case definition** as the
   primary model.
9. The interpretation of residual or interaction Moran's I is deliberately
   conservative. Near-zero residual Moran's I is not treated as proof that the
   spatial model is perfectly specified.

The production primary fit was run on Cornell Seneca HPC using R 4.6.0 and
INLA 26.8.7. The completed 2016-2025 primary panel contains 668,400
municipality-month observations (5,570 municipalities x 120 months).

# 1. Municipality shapefile and adjacency graph

For reproducibility, use the same 2020 municipality ordering that was used to
construct the stored adjacency graph.

```{r shapefile-adjacency}
if (file.exists(result_path("muni_sf_2020.rds"))) {
  muni_sf <- readRDS(result_path("muni_sf_2020.rds"))
} else {
  muni_sf <- read_municipality(year = 2020) %>%
    st_make_valid()
}

muni_sf <- muni_sf %>%
  mutate(
    code_muni = substr(as.character(code_muni), 1, 6),
    code_muni = str_pad(code_muni, width = 6, pad = "0")
  )

space_levels <- muni_sf$code_muni

stopifnot(length(space_levels) == nrow(muni_sf))
stopifnot(length(space_levels) == 5570L)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(space_levels))

if (file.exists(result_path("brazil_muni_2020.adj"))) {
  g <- INLA::inla.read.graph(result_path("brazil_muni_2020.adj"))
} else {
  nb <- poly2nb(muni_sf, queen = TRUE)
  adj_file <- result_path("brazil_muni_2020.adj")
  nb2INLA(file = adj_file, nb = nb)
  g <- INLA::inla.read.graph(adj_file)
}

nb <- poly2nb(muni_sf, queen = TRUE)
lw <- nb2listw(nb, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)

cat("Municipalities:", length(space_levels), "\n")
```

# 2. Build the complete 2016-2025 municipality-month panel

The revised panel is constructed **from the complete municipality x month grid
first**, then confirmed case counts are joined onto it.

This is important. A municipality-month with no confirmed SINAN record is a
reported count of zero for the count model; it is not a missing observation.
Building the panel from observed cases first would select municipalities on the
outcome and would silently remove municipalities with no confirmed cases over a
period.

```{r panel-function}
make_panel_muni_month_pop <- function(
  dat,
  pop_panel_total,
  space_levels,
  start_date = "2016-01-01",
  end_date   = "2025-12-01"
) {

  all_months <- seq(
    as.Date(start_date),
    as.Date(end_date),
    by = "month"
  )

  full_panel <- tidyr::crossing(
    code_muni = space_levels,
    ym_date   = all_months
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      ym   = format(ym_date, "%Y-%m"),
      year = lubridate::year(ym_date)
    )

  observed_cases <- dat %>%
    transmute(
      code_muni = substr(as.character(ID_MUNICIP), 1, 6),
      code_muni = str_pad(code_muni, width = 6, pad = "0"),
      ym_date    = floor_date(as.Date(DT_SIN_PRI), unit = "month"),
      is_conf    = CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13)
    ) %>%
    filter(
      is_conf,
      !is.na(code_muni),
      !is.na(ym_date),
      ym_date >= as.Date(start_date),
      ym_date <= as.Date(end_date),
      code_muni %in% space_levels
    ) %>%
    count(code_muni, ym_date, name = "cases")

  panel <- full_panel %>%
    left_join(observed_cases, by = c("code_muni", "ym_date")) %>%
    mutate(cases = replace_na(cases, 0L)) %>%
    left_join(pop_panel_total, by = c("code_muni", "year")) %>%
    rename(POP = total_pop) %>%
    filter(!is.na(POP), POP > 0) %>%
    mutate(
      space = match(code_muni, space_levels),
      time  = match(ym_date, all_months)
    )

  n_space <- length(space_levels)

  panel <- panel %>%
    mutate(
      st_id = (time - 1L) * n_space + space
    )

  # Hard checks for the revised analysis.
  stopifnot(length(all_months) == 120L)
  stopifnot(n_distinct(panel$code_muni) == 5570L)
  stopifnot(n_distinct(panel$time) == 120L)
  stopifnot(nrow(panel) == 5570L * 120L)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(panel$space))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(panel$time))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(panel$POP))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(panel$cases))
  stopifnot(min(panel$st_id) == 1L)
  stopifnot(max(panel$st_id) == 668400L)

  panel
}
```

```{r build-panel}
panel_chik_2016_2025 <- make_panel_muni_month_pop(
  Chik_total,
  pop_panel_total,
  space_levels
)

cat("Rows:", nrow(panel_chik_2016_2025), "\n")
cat("Municipalities:", n_distinct(panel_chik_2016_2025$space), "\n")
cat("Months:", n_distinct(panel_chik_2016_2025$time), "\n")
cat("Max st_id:", max(panel_chik_2016_2025$st_id), "\n")
cat("Confirmed cases:", sum(panel_chik_2016_2025$cases), "\n")

if (params$run_heavy_models) {
  saveRDS(
    panel_chik_2016_2025,
    file.path(results_dir, "panel_chik_2016_2025.rds")
  )
}
```

- 5,570 municipalities

- 1,215,074 confirmed chikungunya cases

# 3. Primary INLA model

The final primary specification is:

\[
Y_{it} \sim \mathrm{NegBin}(\mu_{it})
\]

with

\[
\log(\mu_{it}) =
\alpha +
\beta_{\mathrm{pop}}\log(POP_{it}) +
u_i +
v_t +
\delta_{it}.
\]

Here:

- `u_i` is the BYM2 spatial main effect;
- `v_t` is a monthly RW2 temporal main effect;
- `delta_it` is a municipality-month IID interaction
  (Knorr-Held Type I);
- the coefficient of `log(POP)` is **estimated**, not fixed at 1.

```{r primary-formula}
formula_chik <- cases ~
  log(POP) +
  f(
    space,
    model = "bym2",
    graph = g,
    scale.model = TRUE,
    hyper = list(
      prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01)),
      phi  = list(prior = "pc",      param = c(0.5, 2/3))
    )
  ) +
  f(
    time,
    model = "rw2",
    constr = TRUE,
    hyper = list(
      prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01))
    )
  ) +
  f(
    st_id,
    model = "iid",
    hyper = list(
      prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(2, 0.01))
    )
  )
```

## 3.1 Primary model summary

```{r primary-summary}
cat("=== Fixed effects ===\n")
print(
  fit_chik_nb$summary.fixed[
    ,
    c("mean", "sd", "0.025quant", "0.5quant", "0.975quant")
  ]
)

cat("\n=== Hyperparameters ===\n")
print(
  fit_chik_nb$summary.hyperpar[
    ,
    c("mean", "sd", "0.025quant", "0.5quant", "0.975quant")
  ]
)

cat("\nDIC:", fit_chik_nb$dic$dic, "\n")
cat("WAIC:", fit_chik_nb$waic$waic, "\n")
```

The completed Seneca production fit gave:

- `log(POP)` = 1.242 (95% CrI 1.198 to 1.287)
- negative-binomial size = 0.169
- BYM2 `phi` = 0.788
- temporal precision = 3.823
- Type I interaction precision = 0.564
- DIC = 476,168.7
- WAIC = 473,989.6

The estimated population coefficient is therefore not treated as an offset.
The small negative-binomial size parameter indicates substantial
overdispersion.

# 4. Extract fitted incidence rates

The fitted mean is aligned row-for-row with the data supplied to INLA.
Incidence rates are therefore obtained from fitted expected cases divided by
the observed municipality-year population.

```{r extract-lograte-function}
extract_total_lograte <- function(fit_obj, panel_df, per = 1e5) {

  stopifnot(
    nrow(panel_df) ==
      nrow(fit_obj$summary.fitted.values)
  )

  panel_df %>%
    mutate(
      fitted_cases = fit_obj$summary.fitted.values$mean,
      rate_per_person = fitted_cases / POP,
      log_rate_per_person = log(rate_per_person),
      rate_per = rate_per_person * per,
      log_rate_per = log(rate_per),
      ym_date = as.Date(ym_date)
    )
}
```

```{r primary-rates}
st_rate_chik <- extract_total_lograte(
  fit_chik_nb,
  panel_chik_full,
  per = 1e5
)
```

# 5. Relative incidence by macro-region

Relative incidence is summarized against the national municipality-median
fitted incidence in each month.

```{r irr-by-region}
nat_rate_median <- st_rate_chik %>%
  group_by(ym_date) %>%
  summarise(
    nat_rate = median(rate_per, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

st_rate_chik_region <- st_rate_chik %>%
  mutate(code_state = substr(code_muni, 1, 2)) %>%
  left_join(state_region_lookup, by = "code_state") %>%
  filter(!is.na(region)) %>%
  left_join(nat_rate_median, by = "ym_date") %>%
  mutate(
    IRR = rate_per / nat_rate,
    log_IRR = log(IRR)
  )

st_rate_chik_region$region <- factor(
  st_rate_chik_region$region,
  levels = c(
    "North", "Northeast", "Center-West",
    "Southeast", "South"
  )
)

region_time_irr <- st_rate_chik_region %>%
  group_by(region, ym_date) %>%
  summarise(
    median_logIRR = median(log_IRR, na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_high = mean(IRR > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

region_year_irr <- st_rate_chik_region %>%
  mutate(year = lubridate::year(ym_date)) %>%
  group_by(region, year) %>%
  summarise(
    median_logIRR = median(log_IRR, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r irr-plots}
ggplot(region_time_irr, aes(x = ym_date, y = region, fill = median_logIRR)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "log(IRR)\nvs national median"
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(
    title = "Chikungunya Relative Incidence by Macro-region",
    subtitle = "Monthly, relative to the national municipality median",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggplot(region_time_irr, aes(x = ym_date, y = median_logIRR, color = region)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(
    title = "Temporal Trends in Relative Incidence by Macro-region",
    x = "Year",
    y = "log(IRR)",
    color = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

# 6. Municipality x time heatmap

```{r muni-time-heatmaps}
q_rate <- quantile(
  st_rate_chik$log_rate_per,
  c(0.01, 0.99),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

muni_lat <- muni_sf %>%
  mutate(
    pt = st_point_on_surface(geometry),
    lat = st_coordinates(pt)[, 2]
  ) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(code_muni, lat)

st_rate_chik_lat <- st_rate_chik %>%
  left_join(muni_lat, by = "code_muni") %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat))

muni_order_lat <- st_rate_chik_lat %>%
  distinct(code_muni, lat) %>%
  arrange(lat) %>%
  pull(code_muni)

st_rate_chik_lat <- st_rate_chik_lat %>%
  mutate(
    code_muni_lat = factor(
      code_muni,
      levels = muni_order_lat
    )
  )

ggplot(
  st_rate_chik_lat,
  aes(
    x = ym_date,
    y = code_muni_lat,
    fill = log_rate_per
  )
) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    midpoint = median(
      st_rate_chik_lat$log_rate_per,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    limits = q_rate,
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = "log incidence\nper 100k"
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(
    title = "Modeled Chikungunya Incidence Across Municipalities",
    subtitle = "Municipalities ordered south-to-north by latitude",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Municipality"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )
```

# 7. Spatial, temporal, and Type I interaction effects

For BYM2, retain only the municipality-indexed block of the returned random
effect when mapping the combined spatial effect.

```{r random-effects}
n_space <- length(space_levels)

spatial_raw <- fit_chik_nb$summary.random$space

spatial_effect <- spatial_raw %>%
  filter(ID <= n_space) %>%
  transmute(
    space = ID,
    spatial_mean = mean,
    code_muni = space_levels[space]
  )

muni_spatial <- muni_sf %>%
  left_join(spatial_effect, by = "code_muni")

ggplot(muni_spatial) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = spatial_mean), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Spatial effect"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "BYM2 Spatial Effect",
    subtitle = "Persistent municipality-level spatial structure"
  ) +
  theme_void()

temporal_effect <- fit_chik_nb$summary.random$time %>%
  transmute(
    time = ID,
    temporal_mean = mean
  )

time_lookup <- panel_chik_full %>%
  distinct(time, ym_date) %>%
  arrange(time)

temporal_effect <- temporal_effect %>%
  left_join(time_lookup, by = "time")

ggplot(temporal_effect, aes(x = ym_date, y = temporal_mean)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly RW2 Temporal Effect",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Temporal random effect"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

interaction_effect <- fit_chik_nb$summary.random$st_id %>%
  transmute(
    st_id = ID,
    interaction_mean = mean
  )

st_interaction <- panel_chik_full %>%
  select(code_muni, ym_date, time, space, st_id) %>%
  left_join(interaction_effect, by = "st_id") %>%
  left_join(muni_lat, by = "code_muni") %>%
  mutate(
    code_muni_lat = factor(
      code_muni,
      levels = muni_order_lat
    )
  )

q_int <- quantile(
  st_interaction$interaction_mean,
  c(0.01, 0.99),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

ggplot(
  st_interaction,
  aes(
    x = ym_date,
    y = code_muni_lat,
    fill = interaction_mean
  )
) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = q_int,
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Type I\ninteraction"
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(
    title = "Municipality-Month Type I Interaction",
    subtitle = "Residual municipality-specific deviations after main space/time effects",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Municipality"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )
```

# 8. Moran's I of the Type I interaction

A positive Moran's I in an IID interaction should **not** be interpreted as
evidence that the Type I interaction is correctly specified. It indicates that
the fitted interaction still contains spatially structured pattern. This is why
the Center-West Type IV sensitivity analysis is retained below.

```{r morans-i-interaction}
monthly_moran_interaction <- lapply(
  sort(unique(st_interaction$time)),
  function(tt) {

    vals <- st_interaction %>%
      filter(time == tt) %>%
      arrange(space) %>%
      pull(interaction_mean)

    mt <- moran.test(
      vals,
      lw,
      zero.policy = TRUE
    )

    data.frame(
      time = tt,
      ym_date = min(
        st_interaction$ym_date[
          st_interaction$time == tt
        ]
      ),
      moran_I = unname(
        mt$estimate["Moran I statistic"]
      ),
      expectation = unname(
        mt$estimate["Expectation"]
      ),
      p_value = mt$p.value
    )
  }
) %>%
  bind_rows()

ggplot(
  monthly_moran_interaction,
  aes(x = ym_date, y = moran_I)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Global Moran's I of the Type I Interaction",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Moran's I"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

summary(monthly_moran_interaction$moran_I)
```

# 9. Local Moran's I (time-averaged interaction)

```{r lisa}
muni_avg_interaction <- st_interaction %>%
  group_by(code_muni, space) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_int = mean(interaction_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(space)

lisa_vals <- muni_avg_interaction$mean_int

local_m <- localmoran(
  lisa_vals,
  lw,
  zero.policy = TRUE
)

muni_lisa <- muni_sf %>%
  mutate(
    local_I = local_m[, 1],
    local_p = local_m[, 5],
    mean_int = lisa_vals
  )

mean_val <- mean(lisa_vals)
lag_val <- lag.listw(
  lw,
  lisa_vals,
  zero.policy = TRUE
)

muni_lisa <- muni_lisa %>%
  mutate(
    quad = case_when(
      mean_int > mean_val &
        lag_val > mean_val &
        local_p < 0.05 ~ "HH",
      mean_int < mean_val &
        lag_val < mean_val &
        local_p < 0.05 ~ "LL",
      mean_int > mean_val &
        lag_val < mean_val &
        local_p < 0.05 ~ "HL",
      mean_int < mean_val &
        lag_val > mean_val &
        local_p < 0.05 ~ "LH",
      TRUE ~ "Not sig."
    ),
    quad = factor(
      quad,
      levels = c(
        "HH", "LL", "HL", "LH", "Not sig."
      )
    )
  )

states_diss <- muni_lisa %>%
  mutate(
    code_state = substr(code_muni, 1, 2)
  ) %>%
  group_by(code_state) %>%
  summarise(.groups = "drop")

ggplot(muni_lisa) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = quad), color = NA) +
  geom_sf(
    data = states_diss,
    fill = NA,
    linewidth = 0.3,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Local Moran's I of Time-Averaged Type I Interaction",
    subtitle = "HH = high-high; LL = low-low"
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

# 10. Sensitivity analysis 1: Poisson likelihood

This sensitivity changes only the observation likelihood. The spatial,
temporal, interaction, population, study-period, and prior specifications are
otherwise unchanged.

```{r poisson-comparison}
poisson_path <- file.path(
  results_dir,
  "fit_chik_poisson_2016_2025.rds"
)

if (file.exists(poisson_path)) {
  fit_chik_poisson <- readRDS(poisson_path)

  model_comparison <- data.frame(
    quantity = c(
      "log(POP)",
      "Space precision",
      "BYM2 phi",
      "Time precision",
      "Type I precision",
      "DIC",
      "WAIC"
    ),
    NB = c(
      fit_chik_nb$summary.fixed["log(POP)", "mean"],
      fit_chik_nb$summary.hyperpar["Precision for space", "mean"],
      fit_chik_nb$summary.hyperpar["Phi for space", "mean"],
      fit_chik_nb$summary.hyperpar["Precision for time", "mean"],
      fit_chik_nb$summary.hyperpar["Precision for st_id", "mean"],
      fit_chik_nb$dic$dic,
      fit_chik_nb$waic$waic
    ),
    Poisson = c(
      fit_chik_poisson$summary.fixed["log(POP)", "mean"],
      fit_chik_poisson$summary.hyperpar["Precision for space", "mean"],
      fit_chik_poisson$summary.hyperpar["Phi for space", "mean"],
      fit_chik_poisson$summary.hyperpar["Precision for time", "mean"],
      fit_chik_poisson$summary.hyperpar["Precision for st_id", "mean"],
      fit_chik_poisson$dic$dic,
      fit_chik_poisson$waic$waic
    )
  )

  print(model_comparison)
}
```

The completed Poisson sensitivity gave:

- `log(POP)` = 1.113 (95% CrI 1.070 to 1.156)
- BYM2 `phi` = 0.793
- temporal precision = 3.890
- Type I precision = 0.145
- DIC = 799,060.7
- WAIC = 1,864,397

The spatial mixing parameter and temporal precision were very similar to the
negative-binomial fit. In contrast, the Poisson model required much larger
municipality-month interaction variance (lower interaction precision), which
is consistent with the IID interaction absorbing extra-Poisson variability.
Information criteria were also substantially poorer under Poisson.

Because the model contains a municipality-month latent interaction, WAIC is
interpreted cautiously and is not used as the sole basis for likelihood choice.
The strong overdispersion estimate in the negative-binomial model and the
increase in interaction variance under Poisson are considered jointly.

# 12. Sensitivity analysis 3: Center-West Type I versus Type IV

The comparison is restricted to Center-West to keep the structured
space-time sensitivity computationally tractable.

Both models must contain the **same spatial and temporal main effects**.
The only intended difference is the interaction structure:

- Type I: unstructured municipality-month IID interaction;
- Type IV: structured space x structured time interaction.

The old grouped-BYM2 implementation is not used here because it does not give
a clean comparison in which only the interaction structure changes.

```{r centerwest-subgraph}
cw_states <- c("50", "51", "52", "53")

muni_sf_cw <- muni_sf %>%
  filter(
    substr(code_muni, 1, 2) %in% cw_states
  )

space_levels_cw <- muni_sf_cw$code_muni
n_space_cw <- length(space_levels_cw)

nb_cw <- poly2nb(
  muni_sf_cw,
  queen = TRUE
)

adj_file_cw <- tempfile(fileext = ".adj")
nb2INLA(
  file = adj_file_cw,
  nb = nb_cw
)

g_cw <- INLA::inla.read.graph(adj_file_cw)

panel_chik_cw <- panel_chik_2016_2025 %>%
  filter(
    code_muni %in% space_levels_cw
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    space_cw = match(
      code_muni,
      space_levels_cw
    ),
    time_cw = time,
    st_id_cw =
      (time_cw - 1L) *
      n_space_cw +
      space_cw
  ) %>%
  arrange(time_cw, space_cw)

stopifnot(
  n_distinct(panel_chik_cw$time_cw) == 120L
)
```

# 13. Primary model diagnostics

## 13.1 Negative-binomial Pearson residuals

For the fitted negative-binomial parameterization:

\[
\mathrm{Var}(Y) =
\mu + \frac{\mu^2}{k},
\]

where `k` is the reported negative-binomial size parameter.

```{r diagnostics-residuals}
size_row <- grep(
  "^size for the nbinomial observations",
  rownames(fit_chik_nb$summary.hyperpar),
  value = TRUE
)

stopifnot(length(size_row) == 1L)

nb_size <- fit_chik_nb$summary.hyperpar[
  size_row,
  "mean"
]

panel_with_resid <- panel_chik_full %>%
  mutate(
    fitted =
      fit_chik_nb$summary.fitted.values$mean,
    resid_raw =
      cases - fitted,
    resid_pearson =
      resid_raw /
      sqrt(
        fitted +
        fitted^2 / nb_size
      )
  )

resid_by_muni <- panel_with_resid %>%
  group_by(space, code_muni) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_resid =
      mean(
        resid_pearson,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(space)

moran_resid <- moran.test(
  resid_by_muni$mean_resid,
  lw,
  zero.policy = TRUE
)

print(moran_resid)
```

Interpretation should remain conservative. Because the model contains one IID
interaction term for every municipality-month, near-zero residual spatial
autocorrelation is descriptive evidence only; it is **not** proof that the
spatial model captured every relevant spatial process.

```{r residual-map}
resid_map_data <- muni_sf %>%
  left_join(
    resid_by_muni %>%
      select(code_muni, mean_resid),
    by = "code_muni"
  )

ggplot(resid_map_data) +
  geom_sf(
    aes(fill = mean_resid),
    color = NA
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Mean Pearson\nresidual"
  ) +
  labs(
    title =
      "Time-Averaged Negative-Binomial Pearson Residuals"
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

## 13.3 CPO/PIT

CPO/PIT are **not part of the production primary fit** in this revision.
The main fit uses `cpo = FALSE`.

If CPO/PIT are needed for the final revision, they should be run as a separate
HPC job rather than making the primary fit dependent on successful CPO result
collection. Previous attempts at this scale showed that model estimation could
finish while CPO result collection itself failed. This is reported as a
computational limitation rather than being treated as evidence for or against
the model specification.

# 14. Absolute-incidence sanity checks

These checks use the **same confirmed-case definition** as the model:
`CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13)`.

The revised analysis period begins in 2016, so the Northeast check is shown for
2016-2017 rather than 2015-2017.

```{r absolute-incidence-checks}
northeast_states <- c(
  "21", "22", "23", "24", "25",
  "26", "27", "28", "29"
)

ne_pop_by_year <- pop_panel_total %>%
  filter(
    substr(code_muni, 1, 2) %in%
      northeast_states
  ) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    ne_pop =
      sum(total_pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ne_cases_by_year <- Chik_total %>%
  transmute(
    year =
      lubridate::year(
        as.Date(DT_SIN_PRI)
      ),
    code_state =
      substr(
        as.character(ID_MUNICIP),
        1, 2
      ),
    is_conf =
      CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    is_conf,
    code_state %in% northeast_states,
    year %in% 2016:2017
  ) %>%
  count(year) %>%
  left_join(
    ne_pop_by_year,
    by = "year"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    incidence_per_100k =
      n / ne_pop * 1e5
  )

print(ne_cases_by_year)

cw_states <- c("50", "51", "52", "53")

cw_pop_by_year <- pop_panel_total %>%
  filter(
    substr(code_muni, 1, 2) %in%
      cw_states
  ) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    cw_pop =
      sum(total_pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cw_cases_by_year <- Chik_total %>%
  transmute(
    year =
      lubridate::year(
        as.Date(DT_SIN_PRI)
      ),
    code_state =
      substr(
        as.character(ID_MUNICIP),
        1, 2
      ),
    is_conf =
      CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    is_conf,
    code_state %in% cw_states,
    year %in% 2024:2025
  ) %>%
  count(year) %>%
  left_join(
    cw_pop_by_year,
    by = "year"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    incidence_per_100k =
      n / cw_pop * 1e5
  )

print(cw_cases_by_year)
```

# 15. Computational provenance and development record

This section documents the major decisions made while revising the analysis.
It is intended for reproducibility and internal revision tracking, not
necessarily for inclusion in the manuscript.

## 15.1 Full 2015-2025 model troubleshooting

The original full analysis window contained 132 months:

- 5,570 municipalities
- 132 months
- 735,240 municipality-month observations
- 735,240 Type I interaction levels

The full 2015-2025 model repeatedly failed in the INLA backend despite multiple
diagnostic changes.

The following checks were performed during troubleshooting:

- shorter windows such as 2015 only, 2015-2017, and 2015-2022;
- 2015-2024;
- 2016-2025;
- a lean fit with DIC/WAIC and additional outputs disabled;
- a newer INLA installation under R 4.6.0;
- warm-starting from the successful 2016-2025 mode;
- fixing the hyperparameters at the 2016-2025 estimates;
- a full Poisson model with the same Type I interaction;
- threshold-size experiments between 120 and 132 months.

The important conclusion from those checks was that the failure could not be
explained simply by RAM, the negative-binomial likelihood, DIC/WAIC output, or
poor hyperparameter initialization. The full 132-month latent interaction was
the persistent computational difficulty.

The revised analysis therefore uses the fixed 2016-2025 period, which preserves
10 complete calendar years and the original monthly Type I interaction
structure.

## 15.2 Successful production run

The revised primary model was successfully completed on Seneca:

- 668,400 municipality-month observations
- elapsed time approximately 2 h 46 min
- peak memory approximately 15.8 GB
- exit code 0
- R 4.6.0
- INLA 26.8.7

The earlier diagnostic 2016-2025 fit and the clean revised production fit both
completed at essentially the same scale and runtime, supporting the stability
of the 120-month analysis.

## 15.3 Model interpretation decisions

The following interpretation rules are retained throughout the revision:

- zero confirmed-case municipality-months are modeled as `0`, not `NA`;
- population is not treated as an offset;
- the Type I interaction is not removed merely to reduce computational cost;
- persistent spatial autocorrelation in an IID interaction is treated as a
  reason for a structured-interaction sensitivity analysis, not as validation
  of the IID interaction;
- residual Moran's I is interpreted cautiously because the model contains a
  municipality-month latent effect;
- DIC/WAIC are compared across sensitivity models but are not interpreted in
  isolation, particularly when an observation-level latent interaction is
  present.


# 16. Reviewer-facing Bayesian validation package

This section consolidates the Bayesian-model validation work added during the
revision. It is intentionally kept in the INLA file because all of these checks
depend directly on the primary INLA fit.

The package includes:

- a complete posterior parameter table;
- prior-versus-posterior plots for the random-effect standard deviations;
- area-averaged negative-binomial Pearson residuals;
- a formal residual Moran's I test;
- monthly Moran's I for the Type I interaction;
- observed-versus-fitted sanity checks;
- Poisson likelihood sensitivity;
- exclusion of 2020-2021;
- the structured-interaction sensitivity workflow;
- documentation of the CPO/PIT attempts and their computational limitation;
- computation time and software environment.

## 16.1 Complete posterior parameter table

```{r reviewer-parameter-table}
fixed_tab <- fit_chik_nb$summary.fixed %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("parameter") %>%
  select(
    parameter,
    mean,
    sd,
    `0.025quant`,
    `0.5quant`,
    `0.975quant`
  )

hyper_tab <- fit_chik_nb$summary.hyperpar %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("parameter") %>%
  select(
    parameter,
    mean,
    sd,
    `0.025quant`,
    `0.5quant`,
    `0.975quant`
  )

cat("=== FIXED EFFECTS ===\n")
print(fixed_tab)

cat("\n=== HYPERPARAMETERS ===\n")
print(hyper_tab)
```

For the revised 2016-2025 primary fit, the principal estimates are:

- intercept: -16.030 (95% CrI -16.465 to -15.596);
- `log(POP)`: 1.242 (95% CrI 1.198 to 1.287);
- negative-binomial size: 0.169;
- spatial precision: 0.235;
- BYM2 mixing parameter `phi`: 0.788;
- temporal precision: 3.823;
- Type I interaction precision: 0.564.

## 16.2 Prior versus posterior: random-effect standard deviations

The final reviewer-facing figure is shown on the **standard-deviation scale**
rather than the precision scale because standard deviations are more directly
interpretable.

For a PC precision prior specified as `pc.prec(u, alpha)`, the implied standard
deviation prior satisfies

\[
P(\sigma > u) = \alpha
\]

and therefore has an exponential density with rate
`-log(alpha) / u`.

The three panels correspond to the spatial heterogeneity scale, temporal RW2
scale, and municipality-month Type I interaction scale.

```{r prior-posterior-sd}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Posterior precision -> posterior standard deviation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

post_space_prec <- fit_chik_nb$marginals.hyperpar[["Precision for space"]]
post_time_prec  <- fit_chik_nb$marginals.hyperpar[["Precision for time"]]
post_st_prec    <- fit_chik_nb$marginals.hyperpar[["Precision for st_id"]]

stopifnot(
  !is.null(post_space_prec),
  !is.null(post_time_prec),
  !is.null(post_st_prec)
)

post_space_sd <- INLA::inla.tmarginal(
  function(tau) 1 / sqrt(tau),
  post_space_prec
)

post_time_sd <- INLA::inla.tmarginal(
  function(tau) 1 / sqrt(tau),
  post_time_prec
)

post_st_sd <- INLA::inla.tmarginal(
  function(tau) 1 / sqrt(tau),
  post_st_prec
)

# PC prior density on the SD scale:
# P(sigma > u) = alpha  -> sigma ~ Exponential(lambda)
pc_sd_density <- function(x, u, alpha) {
  lambda <- -log(alpha) / u
  ifelse(x >= 0, lambda * exp(-lambda * x), 0)
}

make_prior_post_panel <- function(
  posterior_marginal,
  u,
  alpha,
  title,
  x_lab
) {
  post <- as.data.frame(posterior_marginal)
  names(post) <- c("x", "density")

  # Plot over the range supported by the posterior, with modest extension
  # so the PC prior remains visible without allowing its long tail to flatten
  # the posterior display.
  xmax <- max(post$x, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.15
  prior <- data.frame(
    x = seq(0, xmax, length.out = 500)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      density = pc_sd_density(x, u = u, alpha = alpha)
    )

  ggplot() +
    geom_area(
      data = post,
      aes(x = x, y = density),
      alpha = 0.20
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = post,
      aes(x = x, y = density, linetype = "Posterior"),
      linewidth = 0.9
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = prior,
      aes(x = x, y = density, linetype = "Prior"),
      linewidth = 0.8
    ) +
    scale_linetype_manual(
      values = c(
        "Posterior" = "solid",
        "Prior" = "dashed"
      ),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = x_lab,
      y = "Density"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}

p1 <- make_prior_post_panel(
  posterior_marginal = post_space_sd,
  u = 1,
  alpha = 0.01,
  title = "Spatial heterogeneity",
  x_lab = expression(sigma[spatial])
)

p2 <- make_prior_post_panel(
  posterior_marginal = post_time_sd,
  u = 1,
  alpha = 0.01,
  title = "Temporal effect",
  x_lab = expression(sigma[time])
)

p3 <- make_prior_post_panel(
  posterior_marginal = post_st_sd,
  u = 2,
  alpha = 0.01,
  title = "Space-time interaction",
  x_lab = expression(sigma[interaction])
)

fig_prior_post <- p1 + p2 + p3 +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.tag = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 12
    )
  )

fig_prior_post
```

The posterior mean SDs are approximately:

- spatial heterogeneity: 2.07;
- temporal RW2 effect: 0.52;
- Type I space-time interaction: 1.33.

The BYM2 `phi` posterior is reported in the parameter table rather than in this
three-panel SD figure because `phi` is a mixing parameter, not a standard
deviation.

## 16.3 Negative-binomial Pearson residuals

The revised residual definition uses the negative-binomial variance

\[
Var(Y_{it}) = \mu_{it} + \mu_{it}^2/k
\]

rather than the Poisson approximation `sqrt(mu)` used in an earlier exploratory
version.

```{r reviewer-nb-residuals}
size_name <- grep(
  "^size for the nbinomial observations",
  rownames(fit_chik_nb$summary.hyperpar),
  value = TRUE
)

stopifnot(length(size_name) == 1L)

nb_size <- fit_chik_nb$summary.hyperpar[
  size_name,
  "mean"
]

fitted_mean <- fit_chik_nb$summary.fitted.values$mean

stopifnot(
  length(fitted_mean) == nrow(panel_chik_full)
)

panel_with_resid <- panel_chik_full %>%
  mutate(
    fitted = fitted_mean,
    resid_raw = cases - fitted,
    resid_pearson =
      resid_raw /
      sqrt(
        fitted +
        fitted^2 / nb_size
      )
  )
```

## 16.4 Observed-versus-fitted sanity checks

```{r reviewer-observed-fitted-checks}
obs_total <- sum(
  panel_with_resid$cases,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

fit_total <- sum(
  panel_with_resid$fitted,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

cat("Observed total cases:", obs_total, "\n")
cat("Fitted total cases:", fit_total, "\n")
cat("Observed / fitted ratio:", obs_total / fit_total, "\n")

cat(
  "Positive Pearson residual municipality-months:",
  sum(
    panel_with_resid$resid_pearson > 0,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Negative Pearson residual municipality-months:",
  sum(
    panel_with_resid$resid_pearson < 0,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ),
  "\n"
)
```

In the revised production model the observed total was 1,215,074 cases and the
sum of fitted posterior means was approximately 1.08 million. This diagnostic
is retained explicitly because the municipality-month interaction can produce
good local fit while aggregate calibration still deserves inspection.

## 16.5 Area-averaged residual map

Residuals are averaged over the 120 months within each municipality before
mapping.

```{r reviewer-residual-map}
resid_by_muni <- panel_with_resid %>%
  group_by(
    space,
    code_muni
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pearson =
      mean(
        resid_pearson,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(space)

stopifnot(
  nrow(resid_by_muni) == 5570L
)

resid_map_data <- muni_sf %>%
  left_join(
    resid_by_muni %>%
      select(
        code_muni,
        mean_pearson
      ),
    by = "code_muni"
  )

stopifnot(
  sum(is.na(resid_map_data$mean_pearson)) == 0L
)

ggplot(resid_map_data) +
  geom_sf(
    aes(fill = mean_pearson),
    color = NA
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Mean Pearson\nresidual"
  ) +
  labs(
    title =
      "Area-averaged Pearson residuals",
    subtitle =
      "Negative-binomial Pearson residuals, averaged across 2016-2025"
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

## 16.6 Formal test of residual spatial autocorrelation

The municipality order used for residual testing must match the spatial graph
order exactly.

```{r reviewer-residual-moran}
resid_vals <- resid_by_muni %>%
  arrange(space) %>%
  pull(mean_pearson)

stopifnot(
  length(resid_vals) ==
    length(space_levels)
)

moran_resid <- spdep::moran.test(
  resid_vals,
  lw,
  zero.policy = TRUE
)

print(moran_resid)
```

A significant residual Moran's I indicates remaining spatial autocorrelation
after the fitted fixed and random effects. Conversely, a small or non-significant
residual Moran's I should be described only as a diagnostic result; it is not
proof that the spatial specification is uniquely correct.

## 16.7 Monthly Moran's I of the Type I interaction

The Type I interaction is IID by construction. Therefore persistent positive
Moran's I in the posterior interaction field is evidence that the interaction
contains spatially structured pattern, not evidence that the IID assumption is
validated.

```{r reviewer-monthly-interaction-moran}
interaction_effect <- fit_chik_nb$summary.random$st_id %>%
  transmute(
    st_id = ID,
    interaction_mean = mean
  )

interaction_panel <- panel_chik_full %>%
  select(
    st_id,
    time,
    ym_date,
    space
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    interaction_effect,
    by = "st_id"
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    time,
    space
  )

monthly_moran <- lapply(
  sort(unique(interaction_panel$time)),
  function(tt) {

    z <- interaction_panel$interaction_mean[
      interaction_panel$time == tt
    ]

    mt <- spdep::moran.test(
      z,
      lw,
      zero.policy = TRUE
    )

    data.frame(
      time = tt,
      ym_date = min(
        interaction_panel$ym_date[
          interaction_panel$time == tt
        ]
      ),
      moran_I = unname(
        mt$estimate[
          "Moran I statistic"
        ]
      ),
      expectation = unname(
        mt$estimate[
          "Expectation"
        ]
      ),
      p_value = mt$p.value
    )
  }
) %>%
  bind_rows()

ggplot(
  monthly_moran,
  aes(
    x = ym_date,
    y = moran_I
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title =
      "Monthly Moran's I of the Type I interaction",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Moran's I"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

summary(
  monthly_moran$moran_I
)
```

This diagnostic motivates the structured-interaction sensitivity analysis. It
does not by itself determine which interaction structure should be retained.


Completed Poisson sensitivity values:

- `log(POP)` = 1.113 (95% CrI 1.070 to 1.156);
- spatial precision = 0.255;
- BYM2 `phi` = 0.793;
- temporal precision = 3.890;
- Type I interaction precision = 0.145;
- DIC = 799,060.7;
- WAIC = 1,864,397.

The spatial mixing parameter and temporal precision were highly stable. The
Poisson model required much larger Type I interaction variance, consistent with
that latent term absorbing substantial extra-Poisson variation. The
population-scaling coefficient was directionally consistent but smaller under
Poisson, so its magnitude should not be described as likelihood-insensitive.

## 16.9 Prior and posterior interpretation

The prior-posterior figure is intended as a diagnostic of how strongly the data
update the stated PC priors. It should not be interpreted only by visual overlap:
posterior concentration, location, and the transformed SD scale are considered
together.

The BYM2 `phi` parameter is reported separately because it controls the share
of spatial variance attributed to the structured component. In the primary fit
the posterior mean `phi` is approximately 0.79.

## 16.10 CPO/PIT attempt and limitation

CPO and PIT were requested as cross-validatory diagnostics. During development,
large-model CPO collection was attempted separately from the primary production
fit. The INLA backend was able to estimate the model but failed during result
collection for the CPO/PIT output.

For the revised production workflow:

- the primary model is therefore fitted with `cpo = FALSE`;
- failure of CPO result collection is **not** treated as evidence that the model
  fit itself failed;
- CPO/PIT, if retried, should be run as a separate HPC job so that the primary
  model does not depend on successful cross-validation output collection.

A template is retained below but is not evaluated when knitting.

## 16.11 Exclusion of 2020-2021

The exclusion sensitivity uses the same NB likelihood, BYM2 spatial effect,
monthly RW2 temporal effect, freely estimated `log(POP)` coefficient, and Type I
interaction as the primary model.

The 2020-2021 observations are excluded while the RW2 retains the original
calendar-time index. Thus the pandemic interval remains a 24-month gap rather
than being compressed out of the latent time scale.

When the saved exclusion fit is present, the following block compares the
population coefficient, spatial mixing parameter, and spatial field with the
primary model.

```{r reviewer-exclusion-comparison}
excl_path <- file.path(
  results_dir,
  "fit_chik_nb_excl2020_2021.rds"
)

if (file.exists(excl_path)) {

  fit_excl <- readRDS(
    excl_path
  )

  cat(
    "Primary log(POP):",
    fit_chik_nb$summary.fixed[
      "log(POP)", "mean"
    ],
    "\n"
  )

  cat(
    "Excluding 2020-2021 log(POP):",
    fit_excl$summary.fixed[
      "log(POP)", "mean"
    ],
    "\n"
  )

  cat(
    "Primary phi:",
    fit_chik_nb$summary.hyperpar[
      "Phi for space", "mean"
    ],
    "\n"
  )

  cat(
    "Excluding 2020-2021 phi:",
    fit_excl$summary.hyperpar[
      "Phi for space", "mean"
    ],
    "\n"
  )

  spatial_excl <- fit_excl$summary.random$space %>%
    filter(
      ID <= length(space_levels)
    ) %>%
    transmute(
      space = ID,
      spatial_mean_excl = mean,
      code_muni =
        space_levels[space]
    )

  spatial_compare <- spatial_effect %>%
    select(
      code_muni,
      spatial_mean
    ) %>%
    inner_join(
      spatial_excl %>%
        select(
          code_muni,
          spatial_mean_excl
        ),
      by = "code_muni"
    )

  cat(
    "Spatial-effect correlation:",
    cor(
      spatial_compare$spatial_mean,
      spatial_compare$spatial_mean_excl,
      use = "complete.obs"
    ),
    "\n"
  )
}
```


### 16.11.1 Macro-regional shift after excluding 2020-2021

Ana's revision plan asks not only whether the spatial structure is stable, but
also whether the substantive macro-regional reconfiguration remains after
excluding the pandemic-disruption years.

No new INLA fit is required here. The saved exclusion fit is post-processed
with exactly the same fitted-incidence and macro-region definitions used for
the primary model. Comparisons are restricted to the retained calendar years
(2016-2019 and 2022-2025).

The summary reports:

- Pearson correlation of primary versus exclusion-model region-year
  `median_logIRR`;
- Spearman rank correlation of region-year relative-incidence summaries;
- agreement in the highest-relative-incidence macro-region for each retained
  year;
- a compact 2024-2025 table, because the late Central-West expansion is the
  headline geographic shift relevant to the revision.

```{r reviewer-exclusion-macroregion-comparison}
if (file.exists(excl_path)) {

  if (!exists("fit_excl")) {
    fit_excl <- readRDS(excl_path)
  }

  panel_excl <- panel_chik_full %>%
    filter(!year %in% c(2020L, 2021L)) %>%
    arrange(time, space)

  stopifnot(
    nrow(panel_excl) ==
      nrow(fit_excl$summary.fitted.values)
  )

  st_rate_excl <- extract_total_lograte(
    fit_excl,
    panel_excl,
    per = 1e5
  )

  nat_rate_median_excl <- st_rate_excl %>%
    group_by(ym_date) %>%
    summarise(
      nat_rate = median(
        rate_per,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  st_rate_excl_region <- st_rate_excl %>%
    mutate(
      code_state =
        substr(code_muni, 1, 2)
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      state_region_lookup,
      by = "code_state"
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(region)) %>%
    left_join(
      nat_rate_median_excl,
      by = "ym_date"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      IRR = rate_per / nat_rate,
      log_IRR = log(IRR),
      year = lubridate::year(ym_date)
    )

  region_year_excl <- st_rate_excl_region %>%
    group_by(region, year) %>%
    summarise(
      median_logIRR_excl =
        median(
          log_IRR,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  region_year_primary_retained <-
    region_year_irr %>%
    filter(
      !year %in% c(2020L, 2021L)
    ) %>%
    transmute(
      region = as.character(region),
      year,
      median_logIRR_primary =
        median_logIRR
    )

  region_year_compare <-
    region_year_primary_retained %>%
    inner_join(
      region_year_excl %>%
        mutate(
          region =
            as.character(region)
        ),
      by = c("region", "year")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      rank_primary =
        min_rank(
          desc(
            median_logIRR_primary
          )
        ),
      rank_excl =
        min_rank(
          desc(
            median_logIRR_excl
          )
        )
    )

  stopifnot(
    nrow(region_year_compare) ==
      5L * 8L
  )

  macroregion_summary <- tibble(
    metric = c(
      "Pearson correlation of region-year median log(IRR)",
      "Spearman correlation of region-year median log(IRR)"
    ),
    value = c(
      cor(
        region_year_compare$
          median_logIRR_primary,
        region_year_compare$
          median_logIRR_excl,
        method = "pearson",
        use = "complete.obs"
      ),
      cor(
        region_year_compare$
          median_logIRR_primary,
        region_year_compare$
          median_logIRR_excl,
        method = "spearman",
        use = "complete.obs"
      )
    )
  )

  print(macroregion_summary)

  top_region_primary <-
    region_year_compare %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    slice_max(
      median_logIRR_primary,
      n = 1,
      with_ties = FALSE
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(
      year,
      top_region_primary = region
    )

  top_region_excl <-
    region_year_compare %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    slice_max(
      median_logIRR_excl,
      n = 1,
      with_ties = FALSE
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(
      year,
      top_region_excl = region
    )

  annual_top_region_compare <-
    top_region_primary %>%
    left_join(
      top_region_excl,
      by = "year"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      same_top_region =
        top_region_primary ==
        top_region_excl
    )

  print(annual_top_region_compare)

  cat(
    "Annual top-region agreement:",
    sum(
      annual_top_region_compare$
        same_top_region
    ),
    "of",
    nrow(
      annual_top_region_compare
    ),
    "retained years\n"
  )

  late_shift_compare <-
    region_year_compare %>%
    filter(year %in% 2024:2025) %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    mutate(
      rank_primary =
        rank(
          -median_logIRR_primary,
          ties.method = "first"
        ),
      rank_excl =
        rank(
          -median_logIRR_excl,
          ties.method = "first"
        )
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(
      year,
      rank_primary
    )

  print(late_shift_compare)

  readr::write_csv(
    region_year_compare,
    file.path(
      results_dir,
      "exclude2020_2021_macroregion_region_year_comparison.csv"
    )
  )

  readr::write_csv(
    annual_top_region_compare,
    file.path(
      results_dir,
      "exclude2020_2021_macroregion_top_region_by_year.csv"
    )
  )

  readr::write_csv(
    late_shift_compare,
    file.path(
      results_dir,
      "exclude2020_2021_macroregion_2024_2025.csv"
    )
  )

  readr::write_csv(
    macroregion_summary,
    file.path(
      results_dir,
      "exclude2020_2021_macroregion_summary.csv"
    )
  )

  cat(
    "\nPandemic-exclusion macro-region comparison complete.\n"
  )
}
```


## 16.12 Structured interaction sensitivity: final workflow

The clean structured-interaction comparison retains the same BYM2 spatial main
effect and RW2 temporal main effect in both models and changes only the
space-time interaction.

The final structured comparison is scoped to Center-West for computational
feasibility.

The preferred implementation is the explicit Knorr-Held Type IV interaction via
`INLA::inla.knmodels(type = 4)`, as shown in Section 12.

An earlier exploratory grouped-BYM2 formulation is archived as development
history only and should not be used for the final Type I versus Type IV
interpretation because it did not isolate the interaction structure as cleanly.

If both final saved Center-West fits are available, compare them here:

```{r reviewer-type1-type4-results}
type1_path <- file.path(
  results_dir,
  "fit_cw_type1_2016_2025.rds"
)

type4_path <- file.path(
  results_dir,
  "fit_cw_type4_2016_2025.rds"
)

if (
  file.exists(type1_path) &&
  file.exists(type4_path)
) {

  fit_cw_type1 <- readRDS(
    type1_path
  )

  fit_cw_type4 <- readRDS(
    type4_path
  )

  type_compare <- tibble::tibble(
    model = c(
      "Center-West Type I",
      "Center-West Type IV"
    ),
    DIC = c(
      fit_cw_type1$dic$dic,
      fit_cw_type4$dic$dic
    ),
    WAIC = c(
      fit_cw_type1$waic$waic,
      fit_cw_type4$waic$waic
    )
  )

  print(type_compare)
}

```

The interaction sensitivity should be interpreted together with convergence and
boundary diagnostics, not by DIC/WAIC alone. The purpose is to determine
whether the substantive spatial conclusions depend on the IID Type I
interaction specification.

# 17. HPC production workflow and model-development record

## 17.1 Final 2016-2025 primary fit

The clean production fit completed successfully on Cornell Seneca:

- R 4.6.0;
- INLA 26.8.7;
- 668,400 municipality-month observations;
- 5,570 municipalities;
- 120 months;
- elapsed time: 2 h 45 min 59 s;
- peak memory: approximately 15.8 GB;
- exit code: 0.

The earlier diagnostic 2016-2025 fit completed in essentially the same runtime,
which provided an independent scale check before the clean production run.

## 17.2 Why the analysis window changed from 2015-2025 to 2016-2025

The original 2015-2025 analysis contained:

- 132 months;
- 735,240 municipality-month observations;
- 735,240 Type I interaction levels.

The full model repeatedly failed at the INLA backend despite extensive
troubleshooting.

The diagnostic sequence included:

- 2015 only;
- 2015-2017;
- 2015-2022;
- 2015-2024;
- 2016-2025;
- disabling DIC/WAIC and other optional outputs;
- upgrading to R 4.6.0 / INLA 26.8.7;
- warm-starting from the successful 2016-2025 hyperparameter mode;
- fixing hyperparameters at the 2016-2025 estimates;
- testing a full Poisson likelihood;
- threshold-size runs between 120 and 132 months.

The full 2015-2025 model failed even with fixed theta and also failed under
Poisson. This made it unlikely that the failure was caused solely by
negative-binomial overdispersion, optional model-fit statistics, poor starting
values, or insufficient RAM.

The revised analysis therefore uses 2016-2025 while preserving the original
monthly Type I interaction rather than changing the scientific model solely to
make the 132-month computation easier.

## 17.3 Zero-case municipality-months

A central data-structure revision was to build the full municipality-month grid
first and then join confirmed cases.

Therefore:

- municipality-months with no confirmed chikungunya record are coded `0`;
- genuine unavailable covariate information remains missing;
- municipalities are not selected into the model based on whether a case was
  observed.

This decision is part of the final analysis, not a computational shortcut.

## 17.4 Population handling

The original offset formulation imposed a population coefficient of exactly 1.
The reviewer correctly identified this as a substantive assumption.

The final model estimates the coefficient of `log(POP)` freely and uses annual
municipality population estimates. The resulting coefficient of 1.242 (95% CrI
1.198-1.287) is inconsistent with proportional scaling, so the revised model
does not use a population offset.

## 17.5 Sensitivity analyses retained in the INLA workflow

The final INLA sensitivity set is:

1. Poisson instead of negative binomial, with all latent components unchanged.
2. Exclusion of 2020-2021 while retaining the original RW2 calendar index.
3. Center-West Type I versus structured Type IV interaction.
4. Residual and interaction spatial-autocorrelation diagnostics.
5. Prior-versus-posterior diagnostics for the PC priors.
6. CPO/PIT attempted separately because full-model result collection was
   computationally unstable.

These analyses are all kept in this INLA Rmd because they are direct validation
or sensitivity checks of the same Bayesian spatiotemporal model.

```{r}
# Figure 3C:
# Change in modeled relative incidence:
# 2024-2025 versus 2016-2017

period_change <- st_rate_chik_region %>%
  mutate(
    period = case_when(
      lubridate::year(ym_date) %in% 2016:2017 ~ "2016–2017",
      lubridate::year(ym_date) %in% 2024:2025 ~ "2024–2025",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(period)) %>%
  group_by(code_muni, period) %>%
  summarise(
    median_logIRR = median(log_IRR, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = period,
    values_from = median_logIRR
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_logIRR =
      `2024–2025` - `2016–2017`
  )

change_sf <- muni_sf %>%
  select(code_muni, geometry) %>%
  left_join(
    period_change,
    by = "code_muni"
  )

q_change <- quantile(
  abs(change_sf$delta_logIRR),
  0.98,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

states_sf_plot <- geobr::read_state(
  year = 2020,
  showProgress = FALSE
)

panel_3C <- ggplot(change_sf) +
  geom_sf(
    aes(fill = delta_logIRR),
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = states_sf_plot,
    fill = NA,
    color = "grey55",
    linewidth = 0.18
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#B2182B",
    mid = "#F7F7F7",
    high = "#2166AC",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-q_change, q_change),
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = expression("Change in log relative incidence")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Change in modeled relative incidence",
    subtitle = "2024–2025 versus 2016–2017"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

panel_3C
```
